title: Image.get_pixel not returning precision-error-free Color
body:
### Tested versions

Tested versions:    4.1.1, 4.5.1, 4.6.3-rc1, 4.7, 4.7.1, and 4.8-dev1
Oldest version:     4.1.1
Newest version:   4.8-dev1

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev1 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GT 1030 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700 CPU @ 3.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.87 GiB memory - WASAPI (192000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Related: #89800

### Context
Suppose you have
```gdscript
var target_color: Color      = any color
var image: Image             = image of any size
```

When you do
```gdscript
image.set_pixel(x, y, target_color)
```

You'd expect `image.get_pixel(x, y)` in the same position to return `target_color` exactly

However, that does not happen due to floating precision errors, which is okay.
Instead, you get something like
```gdscript
target_color           = (0.3198, 0.9311, 0.5963, 0.9209)
image.get_pixel        = (0.3176, 0.9294, 0.5961, 0.9176)
```



### The Problem
When comparing both colors `target_color` and `image.get_pixel` by using `target_color.is_equal_aprox(image.get_pixel(...))` you are expecting to get `true` because it's the exact same color just with a little floating-point variation. The issue is that you do not, even `is_equal_aprox` returns `false` and that is this issue in a nutshell

When using `Image.set_pixel(...)` I expect the color put into that pixel and the one obtained by calling `Image.get_pixel(...)` afterwards on that pixel to be accurately the same. I consider that floating point precision should not be an issue when dealing with this 

### Why in the world would this be a problem?
- A color picker tries to pick a certain pixel but it's not exactly the one registered in a color palette
- A flood-fill algorithm (or bucket-fill) that works within a `while` loop is stuck forever given that it cannot determine that `target_color` and `image.get_pixel(...)` are exactly or `approximately` the same color

### Ideal Fix
`image.get_pixel(...)` returns the exact same color put into it

Lastly, I could fix the infinite loop of flood-fill by making my own comparison with my own tolerance, but I cannot do anything in case of the color picker example given that I would need the exact same color
There should be a way for `target_color` and `image.get_pixel(...)` to be the same (maybe limit `r g b a` values to only 3 decimal places?)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a color
2. Set a certain pixel of an image with that color by using `set_pixel(x, y, color)`
3. Use `image.get_pixel(x, y)` on the same position and to try get that color back
4. You will see they are not the same
 `color == image.get_pixel(x, y)` returns `false` (could be accepted due to imprecision)
 `color.is_equal_aprox(image.get_pixel(x, y))` returns `false` as well, which cannot be accepted

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[new-game-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30029694/new-game-project.zip)
